translations.text: After Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, deported Jeconiah, the rulers, the prisoners, the powerful men, and all the people of the land from Jerusalem, and brought him to Babylon,
and we did not plead before the Lord our God for each of us to turn away from the evil thoughts of his heart.

Now therefore, Lord, God of [?], who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, with signs, wonders, and mighty deeds, and with an uplifted arm, to make this great name for yourself that remains to this day,
we have sinned, acted wickedly, and wronged you, Lord our God. Therefore, upon all your good deeds [?].
As you spoke through Moses your servant on the day when you commanded him to write this law before the children of [?], saying,
“I know that they will not obey me, because they are a stubborn people. They will turn in their hearts in the land to which they have been deported.”
What is [?]? Why, then, are you in the land of your enemies? You have grown old in a foreign land.
Young children have seen the light and have lived on the earth, but they have not known the way of wisdom.
For I have seen the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting brought upon them.
Take courage, then, my children, and cry out to God, who brought these things upon you, and you will be remembered by him.
Look! Your children are coming, those whom you sent away. They are coming, gathered from the east and the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
For God will show the whole earth the light of your radiance.
Your name will be given by God forever: “Peace and Righteousness and the Glory of Devotion to God.”
